rationale: Third candidate, grounded on the accepted map. The TimeoutNow receive handler is the only route that grants the vote-while-a-leader-exists privilege, and it validates nothing beyond the RPC-header version window - it cannot even check currency, because the request carries no term. By contrast requestVote and requestPreVote reject senders outside the configuration, and leadership grants votes despite a leader only when the privilege is set. The claim fixes the attribution responsibility without asserting a violation; reachability by a non-member, the consequence on a healthy leader, and the possibility that the design deliberately trusts leader discipline are all recorded as counterevidence and unknowns. The map gains behavior b-timeout-now and fact f-leader-transfer-privilege, with a new consumer edge on b-vote-campaign; no accepted object's meaning, identity or existing edges change.

b-timeout-now.rationale: New A2 Behavior for the TimeoutNow receive path, which was previously only part of the general authority picture. It records the owner, the absence of any guard beyond the RPC-header window, and the three writes that abandon the current leader context.

f-leader-transfer-privilege.rationale: New A2 Fact for the transfer privilege the code itself calls abusable: pre-vote is skipped and RequestVote carries LeadershipTransfer so peers vote despite having a leader. It is produced by b-timeout-now and consumed by b-vote-campaign; no existing Fact's meaning changes.

b-vote-campaign.rationale: New consumer edge only: the election campaign now records that it reads the transfer privilege to skip pre-vote and set the vote privilege. Its meaning, trigger, producers and other edges are unchanged.

question.question: Is a TimeoutNow request honoured only when its sender is attributed to the receiver's authority context - a voter of the receiver's latest configuration - or can any peer whose RPC header passes the version window make the receiver clear its known leader, enter candidate state and receive the transfer privilege that skips pre-vote and makes peers vote despite having a leader?
question.importance: TimeoutNow is the only route that grants the vote-while-a-leader-exists privilege; the code's own comment says that privilege 'could be abused otherwise' and defends it only by clearing the flag after each election. The receive handler (S49) checks nothing: the request carries only an RPCHeader with no term (S48), and the handler clears the leader, sets Candidate and raises the privilege before a single validation. The vote RPCs by contrast reject a candidate that is not in the configuration and are granted despite a leader only when that privilege is set (S6, S21). If a node that is not a member of the receiver's configuration can reach this handler - a removed server or a stale node still running the same protocol version - it can force term inflation and an election that peers will vote for, which is an authority-transition defect on a core path.
participants: voters that would grant the resulting vote requests
contexts: a peer whose RPC header is within the supported protocol window but is not a voter of the receiver's latest configuration
a receiver that currently has a known leader
event_paths: receiver -> runCandidate (pre-vote skipped) -> electSelf with LeadershipTransfer=true -> peers grant despite a leader

supporting_behavior_ids.b-vote-campaign: Shows what the privilege does: the campaign skips pre-vote and marks its RequestVote as a leadership transfer (S51).
supporting_behavior_ids.b-vote-grant: Shows the other half of the privilege: a voter grants despite a known leader when LeadershipTransfer is set (S6), so the receiver's election is winnable against an established leader.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-leadership-transfer: The legitimate producer of TimeoutNow, which shows the intended authority of the sender and is the contract the receive side does not enforce.

counterevidence: The RPC-header version window is still enforced on this path (S50), so a peer speaking an unsupported protocol version is rejected.
Only a leader drives leadershipTransfer, so under a correct CFT deployment the sender is the current leader; the handler may be relying on that rather than validating it.
The receiver cannot check currency even if it wanted to, because TimeoutNowRequest carries no term (S48); the missing validation may be a design consequence rather than an oversight.

The API doc for LeadershipTransfer states that using transfer leadership is safe in a mixed-version cluster and that an unpromotable follower fails gracefully, which suggests deliberate leniency on the receive side.
unknowns: Whether a peer that is not a voter of the receiver's latest configuration can reach timeoutNow in a legal deployment.
Whether the resulting term inflation or election can unseat a healthy leader rather than merely perturbing terms.
Whether the intended contract is that the receive side trusts the transport/leader discipline, making the correct disposition a documented assumption instead of a duty.
question.trigger_rationale: Reading the leadership-transfer target selection and TimeoutNow wiring exposed a concrete asymmetry rather than a generic untested case: requestVote and requestPreVote both gate on configuration membership (S6, S21), while timeoutNow gates on nothing and the request has no term with which a receiver could check currency (S48, S49). The next action distinguishes whether this is reachable by a non-member in a legal deployment and whether an attributed obligation follows.

obligation.description: A TimeoutNow request is honoured only when its sender is attributed to the receiver's authority context, at minimum a voter of the receiver's latest configuration, so that a peer outside that configuration cannot clear the receiver's known leader, force it into candidate state and hand it the transfer privilege that skips pre-vote and makes other voters grant votes despite having a leader.

scope.description: A Raft node receiving a TimeoutNow request from a peer whose RPC header passes the version window. The obligation concerns the attribution required before the receiver abandons its leader context and raises the transfer privilege, not the election mechanics that follow.
assumptions: The receiver already knows a leader or is otherwise eligible to be asked to campaign.
The version window enforced by processRPC is the only other precondition on this RPC.
excluded: Whether a term should be added to TimeoutNowRequest in future is a protocol-evolution question, not this obligation.
The sender's own behaviour when its transfer fails is out of scope.

pending: Establish whether a non-member sender is reachable in a legal deployment.
Confirm by direct comparison whether an unattributed sender is honoured identically to a legitimate one.

grounding.derivation: S48 shows TimeoutNowRequest carries only an RPCHeader, so no term is available for a currency check; S49 shows the handler taking the full effect with no validation; S50 shows the only preceding guard is the RPC-header version window; S51 shows the privilege's reach (pre-vote skipped, LeadershipTransfer set) and the authors' own note that the privilege 'could be abused otherwise'; S6 and S21 show that the vote RPCs, unlike this handler, reject senders outside the configuration.
grounding.applicability: Applicable to any TimeoutNow reception where the sender is not a voter of the receiver's latest configuration.
unresolved: Reachability of such a sender in a legal deployment.
Whether the design intentionally trusts leader discipline here.
conflicts: The API documentation presents leadership transfer as safe in mixed clusters, while the receive handler grants the highest-privilege election path without the membership check that the vote RPCs apply.
alternatives: If the design is that only a genuine leader ever sends TimeoutNow and the transport is trusted, the correct disposition is a documented assumption plus a comment on the handler, not a violation.

associations.rationale: Locates the unvalidated implementation site (S49), the request shape that lacks a term (S48), the only preceding guard (S50) and the privilege the handler grants (S51).

bindings.description: The TimeoutNow receive handler: it clears the known leader, sets the node to Candidate and raises the transfer privilege, with no term, membership or known-leader validation of the sender.
pending: Confirm that no caller-side filter exists between the transport and this handler.
